title: Can LLMs Improve Their Own Harness? A Controlled Study on ARC-AGI-3
abstract: arXiv:2610.30499v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A generally intelligent system acquires new skills efficiently without requiring humans to redesign its software scaffold for every new task. Yet language models rarely act alone. A harness is a symbolic program that orchestrates calls to the model, handling perception, memory, tool use, recovery, and inference allocation on the model's behalf. ARC-AGI-3 is an interactive benchmark in which agents must explore unfamiliar environments, figure out their goals on the fly, and keep learning as they go. On it, human-steered systems already report ceiling scores across the public games, so we know effective designs exist. We ask whether frontier models can build and improve such a harness on their own. Through a fixed coding bootstrap, each model constructs a complete task harness, acts through that harness on five development games, and revises the entire codebase twice. translated_title: 大语言模型能否改进自身的执行框架？基于ARC-AGI-3的对照研究
translated_abstract: 通用智能系统能够高效地习得新技能，而无需人类为每个新任务重新设计其软件脚手架。然而，语言模型很少单独行动——执行框架是一种符号程序，它代表模型编排各类调用，负责处理感知、记忆、工具使用、异常恢复和推理分配等事务。ARC-AGI-3是一个交互式基准测试，要求智能体探索陌生环境、在行动过程中自主弄清目标并持续学习。在该基准上，由人类引导的系统已经在公开游戏中报告了满分区分数，说明有效的设计是确实存在的。本文提出的问题是：前沿模型能否自行构建并持续改进这样一个执行框架？通过一个固定的编码引导流程，每个模型先构建一个完整的任务执行框架，通过该框架在五个开发游戏上执行任务，并对整个代码库进行两次修订。随后，每个版本都在二十个从未参与过适应过程的留出游戏上进行评估。
tldr: 该论文通过受控实验首次系统考察前沿大语言模型能否自主构建并迭代改进自己的执行框架，让模型在ARC-AGI-3交互式基准上独立编写、使用并两次修订完整框架代码库，再于二十个从未参与改进的留出游戏上检验其泛化能力。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a controlled study on whether frontier LLMs can autonomously build and iteratively improve their own harness, letting models construct, act through, and twice revise a complete harness codebase on the ARC-AGI-3 interactive benchmark, with generalization evaluated on twenty held-out games never used during adaptation.
